shots.description: Establishing: Saltwick Light against an ember-dusk sky, tower brass-edged by the last sun, the dead sea below already sunk in shadow. One gallery pane glints storm-green where the crack catches light. Quiet, warm, ominous only if you know to look.

Wide interior: dusk turns the lamp room to embers and brass. Orla at the bench lays the match tin open with ritual precision; Espen slouches in behind her, spinning the blue saltglass jar between his fingers. The great lens looms honey-dark. She doesn't turn around when she speaks.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: Hands.

shots.description: The scene's grammar established: her salt-cracked hands, knuckles like rope knots, take his — young, quick, smooth — and turn them palms-up in the amber light. The jar is tucked under his arm, still turning slowly. Held close-up; no faces.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: Softer than mine were at eight. Never mind. Watch.

shots.description: Insert: the cracked storm-green pane, hairline whistling thin, the stuffed rag fluttering in the gap. Her finger enters frame and points at it. The six-note figure enters here — note ONE lands exactly on the point. Green sliver of cold in a warm room.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: Minute one: shut the pane. Wind is a thief with patient fingers.

shots.description: The two silhouetted against the dusk glass, cracked pane between them like a third character. On his last line Espen shrugs — stage the shrug as clearly and readably as the crack itself; it is the shot's whole point. Hold on the shrug a beat too long.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: The pane's fine.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: The pane is cracked and you've been told twice.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: It whistles. I like the whistle.

shots.description: Wick scissors snip the charred black beard off the wick — one clean cut. Beside her hands, his mimic the motion a beat late with an invisible pair. The doubling that pays off in scene 8, taught here as choreography. Note TWO of the figure.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: Minute two: trim the wick. Black beard, no flame.

shots.description: Oil rises in the brass reservoir toward a scribed ring; her thumbnail rests exactly on the line as the amber meniscus climbs to meet it and stops. Tilt down follows the pour. His hand hovers, half-attending, jar still turning in the other. Note THREE.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: Minute three: oil to the ring. Not past it, not shy of it.

shots.description: Insert: the open tin. Eight loose matches, counted one by one under her cracked thumb — the rattle is a tiny, dry percussion. Espen's reply comes off-screen, flat, humoring her. Note FOUR lands on the eighth match.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: Minute four: dry hands, dry matches. Say it.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: Dry hands, dry matches.

shots.description: Her eye, ember-lit, unblinking — the stare that has outlasted storms. Off-screen, he says it again, slower this time, and for two words it is almost his. Cutting rhythm slows; let the held close-up do the discipline.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: Say it like it's yours.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: Dry hands. Dry matches.

shots.description: She mimes the strike with a dead match — a long sweep away from the body, dry rasp, no flame. The gesture is exact, muscle-memory old. His hands copy it in the lower corner of frame, sloppy, a beat late. Note FIVE.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: Minute five: strike away from your body.

shots.description: The dying sun lines up through the great lens and floods the room molten amber — a rehearsal of flame, the lamp lit by the sky itself for one breath. Pull back as the caustics crawl across brass and faces. Note SIX lands and hangs unresolved.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: Minute six: burn.

shots.description: The figure stops mid-phrase — the music simply is not there anymore. Two silhouettes against the cooling glass, her back to him. His first question hangs; the second is spoken into her silence. The whistle through the crack is the only voice between them. Slow push toward her still shoulders.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: And if it doesn't?

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: Gran. What happens at minute seven?

shots.description: Her eye again — same framing as before, but now something moves behind it, deep and old. She answers with arithmetic instead of truth, and the shot holds long enough that both of them, and we, know it is not an answer.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: The tin holds eight. Buy more tomorrow.

shots.description: Insert: the stove ledge. The wood worn pale in an exact tin-sized rectangle — a century of matches drying there overnight, generations of the same small obedience. Her hand enters and pats the spot once, like tucking in a child. The figure resumes, muted, dutiful.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: Matches sleep on the stove ledge. Every night. Even when I don't.

shots.description: His hand pockets the tin instead — still damp from the seabed morning, rain ghosting the metal — while the jar keeps spinning in his other hand. Casual, thoughtless, fatal. The line is tossed off over his shoulder.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: Six minutes. It's a lamp, not a heart.

shots.description: The empty pale rectangle holds the frame alone for one long beat. Where the tin should sleep tonight: nothing. The whistle through the cracked pane threads under the silence like water finding a gap. No cut until it aches.

Pattern break: her hand closes on his wrist — hard, older-strong, nothing like the patient teaching hands of the last two minutes. The jar stops spinning. Fast push-in; the first violent cut of the scene.

She guides his fingers into the shadow behind the great lens: a small brass clip, polished by decades of checking, where one match rests alone — dry as a kept promise. Drift around the lens edge as his fingertips find it. His yelp breaks the spell halfway through.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: Behind the great lens. One spare. Dry.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: Ow— fine. One spare. For what?

shots.description: Final frame: her face lit half by ember dusk, half by the storm-green of the cracked pane — the two futures of the episode split down her features. She answers, then opens her mouth on the next sentence — minute seven — and closes it. Hold on the almost-said. Fade out on the whistle.

subs.speaker: ORLA
subs.text: For the night the tin lies to you.
